title: The Nasdaq Just Hit a Correction. What Does That Mean?

scenes.vo: The Nasdaq fell 5.5 percent Thursday, into a correction.
A correction usually means a drop of 10 percent or more from a high. Twenty percent: a bear market.

captions.text: A correction usually means a drop
of 10% or more from a high.

scenes.vo: Its record close was October 6. Thursday, it ended about 12 percent below.
Illustrative: 10,000 dollars tracking the Nasdaq at its peak would be about 8,800 now.
Before reacting, ask: when will I actually need this money?
